turns.t: Mrs Haddad, come through. The doctor's ready for you, and your carer can come in too. ~
Thank you, nurse. Doctor, we've come about the night sweats. They're soaking her bedding.
It's not that bad. A couple of weeks, perhaps.
It's a month at least, Mrs Haddad. I do your washing.
So two weeks from you, a month from Mrs Haddad's side. I'll put it down as two weeks to a month. What are they like?
I wake up drenched. Nightdress wet through, and I have to change. Three or four times a week.
Any fever with it?
No fever. I'd have felt it.
Have you lost weight, without trying?
No. If anything, I've put on a bit.
Any cough, or breathlessness?
No cough.
What medicines do you take?
Just the omeprazole, 20 mg once a day, for her stomach. She has reflux.
And the room, is it warm at night? ~
I put the heating on low for her. She feels the cold. ~
How old are you, Mrs Haddad, if you don't mind? ~
Seventy-two. Why, is it my age? ~
Possibly part of it. I'm not going to guess, I'll do some simple tests first. ~
What kind? ~
A blood test, to check your blood count, thyroid, and inflammation, to rule out any underlying cause.
I can do that for you before you leave, Mrs Haddad. ~
Fine. ~
Meanwhile, keep the bedroom cool, use cotton nightwear and a lighter duvet, and avoid hot drinks and spicy food in the evening.
I'll turn the heating off at night. ~
And keep a diary, how often it happens, and whether you also feel hot in the daytime.
A diary! Well, I can do that, if Aisha helps me. ~
I'd like to see you in two weeks, when the results are back.
We'll be there. Thank you, doctor. ~
This way, Mrs Haddad. ~
